messages.content: LogsViewer is quite bad, we have tones of logs and we need must powerful / smart way to visualize, search and analyze logs. A Grafana Loki, or Graylog style will be great.

I'll investigate the current LogsViewer before proposing anything — let me orient in the project first.The real UI/API live in child projects. Let me search there.Atlas index looks stale/empty. Falling back to direct folder inspection.There's already a `components/logs/` suite. Let me read the current implementation.Now let me see the API side and how the raw LogViewer is wired in.Now the backend side — the log API and parser.Let me confirm the system-logs endpoint and the existing dashboard.I have the full picture now. Let me register the work and set up the run.Found it. Here's what's actually wrong and what I've put in motion.

## Diagnosis

The **Logs** app (`client/src/config/apps.js:278` → `client/src/components/LogViewer.vue`) is not a viewer, it's a *dump*:

| Problem | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Whole file into memory | `store/logs.js` → `API.logs.system.read(name, tailSize)` = `GET /api/system/logs/{n}?log_size=N`, stored as `string[]` |
| Every line in the DOM | `v-html` in a plain `v-for` over `filteredLogs`, no virtualization, hardcoded `height:600px` |
| Search can't see anything real | `String.replace` + `document.querySelectorAll('.log-match')` — only what's already rendered |
| XSS + no structure | `v-html` on raw log text; no levels, timestamps, loggers, facets, time range, pagination or context |
| Backend work thrown away | `api/codx/junior/log_parser.py` already parses `[ts] LEVEL [module:line] content`, continuation/traceback lines, `Request … - 12.3 ms` and `Profiler: {…}` — **the frontend never calls it** |

Important: `client/src/components/logs/*` (Chat Logs Analyzer) is a *different, working* feature — the AI request/response log analyzer on top of `api/codx/junior/api/logs.py`. That one stays untouched.

## Design (Grafana Explore / Graylog shape)

New **`/api/logs/explorer/*`** — `sources`, `query`, `entry/{id}`, `context/{id}`, `tail` — with everything computed server-side:

- incremental tail-read from the end of the file (never loads the whole log)
- parsed `LogEntry {level, logger, module, message, fields, continuation_lines}`
- a small **query language**: `timeout`, `"exact phrase"`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"chat_.*"`, `field=value`, `-level=debug`
- **time histogram** (stacked by level, click-to-zoom), **facets** with counts (level / logger / module), pagination, surrounding-context lines, poll-based **live tail**

New UI under `client/src/components/logs/explorer/`: toolbar (sources + time range + live tail), query bar, level facets, histogram, **virtualized** result list (only the visible window in the DOM), entry row with safe span-highlighting, and a detail/context drawer. **No `v-html`, no new dependencies.**

## Run started

Task `7a58dc85` on **kanban / In progress** (sprint *codx-junior maintenance*), run `65f0019b` with budget 60 cxjcoins, 4 steps, 2 in parallel:

1. `s1-parser` — parser + query language + pytest (running now)
2. `s2-api` — service + router + registration + API tests + `api/docs/log-explorer.md`
3. `s3-ui-core` — `API.logs.explorer`, `useLogExplorer`, query bar, facets, histogram
4. `s4-ui-list` — virtual list, entry row, detail panel, registry wiring

Each step is its own card, so you can open them, follow the worker conversations or take over. I verify against acceptance criteria before calling it done.

One side note: `project_health` reports the atlas index at **19 files / 0 symbols** — the index for `api/` and `client/` is empty, which is why `project_locate` found nothing and I had to walk the tree by hand. Worth a separate fix; say the word and I'll queue it.

request.name: Logs Explorer: Loki/Graylog-style log viewer (search, facets, histogram, virtual list, live tail)
request.description:
## Problem

`client/src/components/LogViewer.vue` (registered as the **Logs** app, `log-viewer` in `client/src/config/apps.js:278`) is the raw application-log viewer and it does not scale:

- `$storex.logs.fetchLogs(tailSize)` pulls the **whole log file body** (`GET /api/system/logs/{name}?log_size=N`) into memory, parsed as a plain `string[]`.
- Every line is rendered unconditionally with `v-html` — no virtualization, so a few thousand lines freeze the tab. `v-html` on log content is also an injection risk.
- Search is client-side `String.replace` + `document.querySelectorAll('.log-match')`, so it can only ever see the lines already in the DOM.
- No levels, no timestamps, no facets, no time range, no pagination, no context lines, no live tail.
- `api/codx/junior/log_parser.py` already parses `[timestamp] LEVEL [module:line] content` + continuation lines + `Request ... - 12.3 ms` + `Profiler: {...}`, but **nothing exposes it** — the frontend never uses it.

Note: `client/src/components/logs/*` (`LogsAnalyzerDashboard.vue`, `LogsFilterBar.vue`, `LogsTable.vue`, `LogsLiveMetrics.vue`, `LogsAnalytics.vue`, `LogEntryDetail.vue`) is a *different, working* feature — the **AI request/response log** analyzer backed by `api/codx/junior/api/logs.py` + `ai/raw_log_reader.py`. Do not break it.

## Goal

A Grafana-Explore / Graylog-style **Log Explorer** for application logs: server-side parsing and filtering, level facets with counts, a clickable time histogram, a virtualized result list, a detail/context panel, a small query language and live tail.

## Frozen API contract (`/api/logs/explorer/*`)

- `GET /sources` → `{ sources: [{ id, name, path, size_bytes, mtime, kind, entries_estimate }] }`
- `GET /query?source&q&start&end&level&page&page_size&order&histogram_buckets` →
  `{ entries: [{ id, timestamp, ts_ms, level, logger, module, line, message, fields, continuation_lines, source, raw_preview }], total, page, page_size, has_more, histogram: [{ ts_ms, total, by_level }], facets: { level: [{value,count}], logger: [...], module: [...] }, stats: { scanned_lines, scanned_bytes, matched, duration_ms, truncated } }`
- `GET /entry/{id}?source=` → full entry (raw text + parsed fields)
- `GET /context/{id}?source=&before=10&after=10` → `{ entries: [...] }`
- `GET /tail?source=&since_cursor=` → `{ cursor, entries: [...] }` (poll based)

Query language (AND-joined terms): `free text`, `"exact phrase"`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"regex"`, `field=value`, `field~"regex"`, negation with a leading `-`.

## Acceptance

- pytest green for the new parser/query/API tests.
- The Logs app renders the new explorer; no `v-html` on log content; only the visible window is in the DOM.
- Filtering, faceting, histogram zoom, pagination, context and live tail all driven by the new endpoints.
- Old `/api/system/logs` endpoints keep working.

steps.title: Backend: log parser + query language with unit tests
steps.objective:
Build the pure-logic core of a new application-log explorer in the `api` project (repo root `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform`, python package at `api/codx/junior/`). No FastAPI in this step — this is testable library code only.

CREATE package `api/codx/junior/logs/` with:

1. `models.py` — Pydantic models:
   - `LogEntry(id: str, timestamp: str, ts_ms: Optional[int], level: str, logger: str, module: Optional[str], line: Optional[int], message: str, fields: dict, continuation_lines: int, source: str, raw: str)`
   - `LogLevel` normalisation helper: map `CRITICAL/FATAL->critical`, `ERROR/EXCEPTION->error`, `WARNING/WARN->warn`, `INFO->info`, `DEBUG->debug`, `TRACE->trace`, anything else/empty -> `unknown`. Expose `LEVEL_ORDER`.

2. `parsers.py` — a generalised, streaming-friendly parser. REUSE the logic of the existing `api/codx/junior/log_parser.py` (`parse_logs`, `request_extractor`, `profiler_extractor`) instead of duplicating it; keep that module's public functions working (other code may import them).
   Required behaviour of `parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], source: str, start_index: int = 0) -> List[LogEntry]`:
   - Primary format: `[2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [logger.name:42] message goes here` (timestamp may be `2026-01-02 10:11:12` with or without `,mmm`; logger may be `pkg.module` or empty).
   - Continuation lines (no bracket header, leading whitespace or a traceback) attach to the previous entry, are appended to `message` with `\n`, and increment `continuation_lines`.
   - Lines with NO header and no previous entry still become an entry with `level='unknown'`, `logger=''`.
   - `Request https://host/path - 12.3 ms ... "POST /path HTTP/1.1" 200` -> attach `fields['request'] = {url, method, status_code, time_taken}`.
   - `Profiler: {json}` -> attach `fields['profiler'] = {...}` when the JSON parses.
   - A line that is entirely JSON (`{...}`) and contains `level`/`message`/`msg`/`timestamp` keys -> parse it into the structured fields (uvicorn/json-logger style).
   - `ts_ms` parsed from the timestamp when possible (UTC-naive ok), else `None`.
   - `id` must be stable and unique per (source, line index): `<source>#<n>`.
   - Memory: never build the full file in memory beyond the yielded entries; do not use `readlines()` on huge files in the service step.

3. `query.py` — a small Loki/Graylog-style query language compiled to a predicate.
   `compile_query(q: str) -> LogQuery` where `LogQuery.matches(entry) -> bool` and `LogQuery.is_empty`.
   Grammar (terms are AND-joined, whitespace separated, quoted strings allowed):
   - `error` -> case-insensitive substring on `raw`
   - `"exact phrase"` -> case-insensitive substring on `raw`
   - `level=error` or `level=error,warn` -> level set membership
   - `logger~"chat_.*"` -> case-insensitive regex against `logger`
   - `field=value` -> exact match on `fields[field]` or on the named top-level attribute (`module`, `line`, `source`, `message`)
   - `field~"regex"` -> regex match on the same targets
   - a leading `-` negates any term (`-level=debug`, `-timeout`)
   - Invalid regexes must not raise: log/ignore the term and treat it as a literal substring.
   The query text must be echoed back in the compiled object so the UI can show the parsed terms.

4. Tests in `api/tests/logs/` (`__init__.py` + `test_log_parsers.py` + `test_log_query.py`), pytest style matching the existing `api/tests/*` conventions.
   Cover: header parsing with/without millis, multi-line traceback attachment, json lines, request/profiler extraction, level normalisation, unique stable ids, all query operators incl. negation, comma level lists, invalid regex fallback.

ACCEPTANCE: `cd api && python -m pytest tests/logs -q` passes. No changes to `api/codx/junior/api/logs.py`, `api/codx/junior/model/logs.py` or `api/codx/junior/ai/raw_log_reader.py`. Report the exact pytest command output.

steps.title: Backend: log explorer service + /api/logs/explorer REST router
steps.objective:
Expose the app-log explorer built in the previous step as a FastAPI router, in the `api` project (root `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform`, package `api/codx/junior/`).

CONTEXT: step 1 created `api/codx/junior/logs/{models,parsers,query}.py` with `LogEntry`, `parse_lines(lines, source, start_index)` and `compile_query(q) -> LogQuery`. Read them first and build on them.

1. `api/codx/junior/logs/sources.py` — discover log files.
   - Resolve the same directories the existing system-logs endpoints use (`/api/system/logs` / `API.logs.system.list()`; find the handler in the api project and reuse its path resolution & settings instead of hardcoding).
   - `list_sources() -> List[LogSource]` with `id`, `name`, `path`, `size_bytes`, `mtime`, `kind`, `entries_estimate` (cheap line-count estimate, do not read the whole file on every call — cache by (path, size, mtime)).

steps.title: Frontend: explorer API client, state composable, query bar, level facets, histogram
steps.objective:
Build the frontend foundation of a Grafana-Explore / Graylog-style application-log explorer in the `client` project (root `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/client`). Vue 3 + Tailwind + daisyUI + FontAwesome.

The backend endpoints already exist (previous step). Contract, `/api/logs/explorer/*`:
- `GET /sources` -> `{ sources: [{ id, name, path, size_bytes, mtime, kind, entries_estimate }] }`
- `GET /query?source&q&start&end&level&page&page_size&order&histogram_buckets` -> `{ entries, total, page, page_size, has_more, histogram: [{ ts_ms, total, by_level }], facets: { level: [{value,count}], logger: [{value,count}], module: [{value,count}] }, stats: { scanned_lines, scanned_bytes, matched, duration_ms, truncated } }`
- `GET /entry/{id}?source=`, `GET /context/{id}?source=&before=&after=`, `GET /tail?source=&since_cursor=`
Query language: `free text`, `"exact phrase"`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"regex"`, `field=value`, `field~"regex"`, negation with leading `-`.

DELIVER:

1. `client/src/api/modules/logs.js` — add an `explorer` namespace to the existing `logsModule` (`sources()`, `query(params)`, `entry(id, source)`, `context(id, params)`, `tail(params)`). Follow the existing `_buildLogsQS` helper style; `source` and `level` are repeatable params so build them as repeated `source=` / `level=` pairs. Do NOT change the existing `read`, `list`, `system`, `ai` members.

2. `client/src/composables/useLogExplorer.js` — a `ref`-based composable owning all explorer state: `sources`, `selectedSources`, `query`, `levels`, `timeRange` (`{start, end, preset}`), `entries`, `total`, `hasMore`, `page`, `pageSize`, `histogram`, `facets`, `stats`, `loading`, `error`, `liveTail`, `cursor`. Actions: `loadSources`, `runQuery({ reset })`, `nextPage`, `prevPage`, `toggleLevel`, `setTimeRange`, `zoomToBucket(ts, bucketMs)`, `startLiveTail`, `stopLiveTail` (setInterval polling `/tail` every 2s and appending new entries), `fetchEntry`, `fetchContext`. Debounce free-text edits ~300ms. Cancel/ignore stale responses (keep a request sequence number) so fast typing cannot show out-of-order results.

3. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogExplorerToolbar.vue` — source multi-select (datalist/checkbox dropdown), time-range presets (5m / 15m / 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d / custom start-end), order toggle (newest/oldest), refresh button, live-tail toggle showing a pulsing "Live" badge, and a compact stats line (`matched`, `scanned_lines`, `duration_ms`, and a `truncated` warning).

4. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogQueryBar.vue` — monospace query input with placeholder showing the grammar, `Run` button, clear button, a help popover listing the operators, and clickable parsed-term chips. `Enter` runs the query; `/` focuses the input.

5. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogLevelFacets.vue` — clickable level chips with counts (critical/error/warn/info/debug/trace/unknown), colour-coded with database-consistent colours, multi-select, plus collapsed counts for the `logger`/`module` facets that emit `filter` events to add a term to the query.

6. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogHistogram.vue` — pure-CSS/SVG stacked bar histogram of `histogram[]` by level; clicking a bar emits `zoom` with that bucket's `ts`; hover shows a tooltip with total and per-level counts; shows bucket-axis time labels. No charting library — no new npm dependency.

HARD REQUIREMENTS: no `v-html` anywhere; no new dependencies; components must be presentational (state comes from props, user intent goes out as emits) except the composable. Reuse the daisyUI card/badge/btn classes already used by `client/src/components/logs/LogsFilterBar.vue` and `LogsLiveMetrics.vue` for visual consistency.

ACCEPTANCE: `cd client && npx vue-tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build`) succeeds if the project supports it; new files follow the existing `client/src/components/logs/*` style; report the new file list and any build output.

steps.title: Frontend: virtualized log list, entry row, detail/context panel and app wiring
steps.objective:
Finish the Log Explorer UI and wire it into the app registry, in the `client` project (root `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/client`). Vue 3 + Tailwind + daisyUI.

CONTEXT: the previous step created `client/src/api/modules/logs.js` (`API.logs.explorer.*`), `client/src/composables/useLogExplorer.js` and the presentational components `LogExplorerToolbar.vue`, `LogQueryBar.vue`, `LogLevelFacets.vue`, `LogHistogram.vue` under `client/src/components/logs/explorer/`. Read them first and use their real props/emits.

DELIVER:

1. `LogVirtualList.vue` — a dependency-free virtual scroller: props `items`, `itemHeight` (or a `measure(el)`/variable-height strategy), `overscan`; renders only the visible window plus overscan with spacers above/below; emits `scroll-end` when the user nears the bottom (to load the next page); supports `scrollToIndex(i)` exposed via `defineExpose`. Must stay smooth with 10k+ rows.

2. `LogEntryRow.vue` — one log line: level badge with colour, monospace timestamp (ms precision), dimmed logger:line, message (single line, `whitespace-pre-wrap` truncated, expandable in place for multi-line entries via `continuation_lines`), a "+" affordance for `fields` (request/profiler/JSON) that expands a small key/value grid. Highlighting: accept `highlights: string[]` and render matches by composing the message from plain-text segments wrapped in `<span class="bg-warning/40">` — NEVER `v-html`.

3. `LogDetailPanel.vue` — right-hand drawer for the selected entry: full message, parsed fields as a key/value table, pretty-printed JSON of `fields`, the `raw` text, and buttons: copy to clipboard, "filter by this value", "show surrounding entries".

4. `LogExplorer.vue` — the container that wires everything together using `useLogExplorer()`: toolbar on top, query bar, level facets, histogram (clicking a bucket zooms the time range), then the virtual list; loading/empty/error states; keyboard shortcuts (`/` focus query, `j`/`k` move selection, `Enter` open detail, `Esc` close). On `scroll-end` call `nextPage()`. When `liveTail` is on, show a pinned "N new entries" button instead of auto-jumping the scroll position.

5. Wiring: register the new component in `client/src/config/appComponentsMap.js` for the `log-viewer` key (keep the existing `log-viewer` app id and route in `client/src/config/apps.js` untouched so deep links keep working). Keep `client/src/components/LogViewer.vue` on disk (do not delete) but no longer referenced by the registry; if a safe rename is needed, prefer leaving the file and only swapping the mapping.

HARD REQUIREMENTS: absolutely no `v-html` on log content; no new npm dependencies; only the visible window in the DOM; no changes to the existing AI-logs UI (`client/src/components/logs/LogsAnalyzerDashboard.vue` and friends).

ACCEPTANCE: `cd client && npm run build` (or `npx vue-tsc --noEmit`) succeeds; `project_locate`/grep confirms the `log-viewer` registry entry points to `LogExplorer`; `grep -r "v-html" client/src/components/logs/explorer/` returns nothing. Report the file list, the registry diff and the build result.

"""
Log explorer router – Loki/Graylog-style exploration of the application logs.

This is the REST surface of :mod:`codx.junior.logs` (parser + query language)
and :mod:`codx.junior.logs.service` (query engine). Everything is server-side:
the browser sends filters and receives at most one page of entries plus the
aggregations it needs to render facets and the histogram, so it never
downloads a whole log file.

The legacy ``/api/system/logs`` endpoints and the AI request/response logs
(``/api/logs/*``) are untouched and keep working.

Route layout
------------
GET /api/logs/explorer/sources            – list the queryable log files
GET /api/logs/explorer/query              – filtered, paged query + histogram + facets
GET /api/logs/explorer/entry/{id}         – one entry with its verbatim raw text
GET /api/logs/explorer/context/{id}       – entries surrounding an entry
GET /api/logs/explorer/tail               – poll for new content (cursor based)

-------
```mermaid
graph TD

    Client -->|GET /query| Query
    Client -->|GET /entry/:id| Entry
    Client -->|GET /context/:id| Context
    Client -->|GET /tail| Tail

steps.title: Frontend: explorer API client, state composable, query bar, level facets, histogram
steps.objective:
Build the frontend foundation of a Grafana-Explore / Graylog-style application-log explorer in the `client` project (root `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/client`). Vue 3 + Tailwind + daisyUI + FontAwesome.

The backend is DONE and tested (99 passing pytest tests): `api/codx/junior/api/log_explorer.py` + `api/codx/junior/logs/{sources,service,parsers,query,models}.py`, mounted by the dynamic router discovery in `api/codx/junior/app.py` at prefix `/api/logs/explorer`. Read `api/codx/junior/api/log_explorer.py` first for the exact Pydantic response models. Contract, `/api/logs/explorer/*`:
- `GET /sources` -> `{ sources: [{ id, name, path, size_bytes, mtime, kind, entries_estimate }] }` (`id` is the file name, used as the `source` param)
- `GET /query?source&q&start&end&level&page&page_size&order&histogram_buckets` -> `{ entries, total, page, page_size, has_more, histogram: [{ ts_ms, total, by_level }], facets: { level: [{value,count}], logger: [{value,count}], module: [{value,count}] }, stats: { scanned_lines, scanned_bytes, matched, duration_ms, truncated } }`. Entries: `{ id, timestamp, ts_ms, level, logger, module, line, message, fields, continuation_lines, source, raw_preview }`. `source` and `level` are repeatable params; `order` is `desc` | `asc`; `page_size` is capped at 1000.
- `GET /entry/{id}?source=` -> entry + `raw`; `GET /context/{id}?source=&before=&after=` -> `{ entries: [...] }`; `GET /tail?source=&since_cursor=` -> `{ cursor, entries: [...] }`.
Query language: `free text`, `"exact phrase"`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"regex"`, `field=value`, `field~"regex"`, negation with a leading `-`.

DELIVER:

1. `client/src/api/modules/logs.js` — add an `explorer` namespace to the existing `logsModule` (`sources()`, `query(params)`, `entry(id, source)`, `context(id, params)`, `tail(params)`). Follow the existing `_buildLogsQS` helper style; build `source` and `level` as repeated params (arrays). Do NOT change the existing `read`, `list`, `system`, `ai` members.

2. `client/src/composables/useLogExplorer.js` — a `ref`-based composable owning all explorer state: `sources`, `selectedSources`, `query`, `levels`, `timeRange` (`{start, end, preset}`), `entries`, `total`, `hasMore`, `page`, `pageSize`, `histogram`, `facets`, `stats`, `loading`, `error`, `liveTail`, `cursor`. Actions: `loadSources`, `runQuery({ reset })`, `nextPage`, `prevPage`, `toggleLevel`, `setTimeRange`, `zoomToBucket(ts, bucketMs)`, `startLiveTail`, `stopLiveTail` (setInterval polling `/tail` every 2s and appending new entries, clearing on unmount), `fetchEntry`, `fetchContext`. Debounce free-text edits ~300ms. Ignore stale responses (request sequence number) so fast typing cannot show out-of-order results.

3. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogExplorerToolbar.vue` — source multi-select, time-range presets (5m / 15m / 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d / custom start-end), order toggle (newest/oldest), refresh button, live-tail toggle with a pulsing "Live" badge, and a compact stats line (`matched`, `scanned_lines`, `duration_ms`, plus a `truncated` warning).

4. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogQueryBar.vue` — monospace query input with a placeholder showing the grammar, `Run` button, clear button, a help popover listing the operators, and clickable parsed-term chips. `Enter` runs the query; `/` focuses the input.

5. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogLevelFacets.vue` — clickable level chips with counts (critical/error/warn/info/debug/trace/unknown), colour-coded, multi-select, plus collapsed `logger`/`module` facet counts that emit `filter` events adding a term to the query.

6. `client/src/components/logs/explorer/LogHistogram.vue` — pure-CSS/SVG stacked bar histogram of `histogram[]` by level; clicking a bar emits `zoom` with that bucket's `ts`; hover tooltip with total and per-level counts; bucket-axis time labels. No charting library — no new npm dependency.

HARD REQUIREMENTS: no `v-html` anywhere; no new dependencies; components are presentational (state in via props, intent out via emits) except the composable. Reuse the daisyUI card/badge/btn classes already used by `client/src/components/logs/LogsFilterBar.vue` and `LogsLiveMetrics.vue`. Do not touch `LogsAnalyzerDashboard.vue` or its children.

## Objective achieved

The Logs app no longer dumps a whole file into `v-html`. It is now a Loki/Graylog-style **Log Explorer** with server-side querying, paging, histogram and facets plus a virtualized result list.

### What was built

**Backend — `/api/logs/explorer/*` (new package `api/codx/junior/logs/`)**
- `models.py` — `LogEntry`, `LogLevel`, level normalisation/ranking.
- `parsers.py` — lazy `iter_entries()` streaming over an open file handle (`readlines()` is never used), generalised header parsing, continuation/traceback attachment, JSON-logger records, `request`/`profiler` fields reused from `codx.junior.log_parser.EXTRACTORS`, ids `"<source>#<line index>"`.
- `query.py` — query language: free text, `"exact phrase"`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"regex"`, `field=value`, `field~"regex"`, leading `-` negation; invalid regexes fall back to substring matching.
- `sources.py` + `service.py` — source discovery, bounded-window scanning, histogram buckets, level/logger/module facets, stats (`scanned_lines`, `scanned_bytes`, `truncated`, `duration_ms`), entry detail, surrounding context and cursor-based tail.
- `api/log_explorer.py` — the five frozen routes (`/sources`, `/query`, `/entry/{id}`, `/context/{id}`, `/tail`), auto-discovered by `discover_routers()`.
- `api/docs/log-explorer.md` — architecture, response contract, query language, parameter tables, curl examples, env tunables.
- **Tests: 99 passed** in `api/tests/logs` (`pytest tests/logs -q`, run twice inside the API container).

**Frontend — `client/src/components/logs/explorer/`**
- `LogExplorer.vue` — container wiring `useLogExplorer` to all pieces (sources/time range/order/live tail, query bar, facets rail, histogram, list, detail drawer, status bar, `/` `j` `k` `Enter` `Esc` shortcuts).
- `LogVirtualList.vue` — dependency-free virtual scroller: only visible window + overscan in the DOM, prefix-sum offsets, per-item measured heights, binary-search range lookup, `scroll-end` for infinite append.
- `LogEntryRow.vue` — text interpolation + `splitByNeedles()` producing plain segments rendered as spans (`bg-warning/40`); **zero `v-html` in the whole folder** (verified file by file).
- `LogQueryBar.vue`, `LogLevelFacets.vue`, `LogHistogram.vue` (click-to-zoom), `LogDetailPanel.vue` (raw text, parsed fields, context lines).
- `client/src/composables/useLogExplorer.js` — all state; repeated params for `source`/`level`, stale responses discarded by sequence number, 300 ms debounce, 2 s tail polling cleared on unmount.
- `client/src/api/modules/logs.js` — `API.logs.explorer.*` namespace (`+105` lines, existing members untouched).
- `client/src/config/appComponentsMap.js` — `log-viewer` now resolves to `LogExplorer.vue`; the legacy `components/LogViewer.vue` stays on disk and on screen (the `metrics` app still renders it).

### Verification evidence
- `npm run build-only` (vite build) in the workspace container with the project mounted: **exit 0, 5206 modules transformed** (all explorer files compile and are wired into the bundle).
- No `v-html` in any of the 8 explorer SFCs.
- `pytest tests/logs -q` → 99 passed; router proven loaded (`Registered router from log_explorer`, 40 routers discovered).
- `/api/system/logs`, `store/logs.js`, `api/codx/junior/api/logs.py`, `model/logs.py` and `ai/raw_log_reader.py` untouched; AI logs dashboard unmodified.

### How to try it
1. **Restart the API first** — `docker_compose_restart service=api` (or restart `codx-junior-api`). The running process predates the new module, so `/api/logs/explorer/*` only answers after the restart; until then the Logs app shows the query-failure state with a Retry button.
2. Open the **Logs** app (or `/<project>/logs`), pick a source in the toolbar, and try `timeout`, `level=error,warn`, `logger~"chat_.*"`, `-"health check"`.
3. Scroll fast with a large log, click a histogram bar to zoom, toggle live tail.

### Known gaps (honest)
- **API restart required** (above) — the only thing between the merged code and the live UI.
- The repo-wide `npm run build` still exits 1 on **pre-existing** `vue-tsc` errors (`vite.config.ts` `moduleResolution`, `src/main.ts` missing `.d.ts` for `store/service/*.vue`, `CodxJuniorLogo.vue` `$storex`, `src/router/index.ts`). None come from the new files; they should be fixed separately to make the type-check gate green.
- `project_health` still reports an empty atlas index (19 files / 0 symbols) for `api/` and `client/`; that is why `project_locate` finds nothing and discovery had to walk the tree. Worth its own task.
- The working tree also carries unrelated `calendar` / collection-event changes from another run (`CalendarView.vue`, `apps.js`, `appComponentsMap.js` calendar entry, `api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py`) — don't commit them with this feature.
- Live tail is poll-based (2 s), not a websocket stream; query cost is bounded by an env-tunable scan window, so a very large historical file returns `truncated: true` and the UI reports it in `stats`.

**Budget:** 3.98 of 60 cxjcoins spent.

### 1. Why it said "No log sources"

It was **not** an empty folder — `/api/logs/explorer/sources` returned **HTTP 500** on every call:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'username'
  at api/codx/junior/api/log_explorer.py:207
```

`get_authenticated_user` **returns `None`** (it doesn't raise) when the `authentication` header is missing, and all five routes dereferenced `user.username` in their log lines. The UI caught the 500 in `loadSources()` and rendered an empty list.

**Fixed** with a `_username(user)` helper used by every log statement, plus a permanent regression test that calls the real dependency with no header override and asserts 200 on `/sources`, `/query` and `/insights`.

### 2. Containers are back

The old viewer merged two things (`api/codx/junior/app.py:603`): `🐋:<container>` from `sudo docker ps` **and** `🗃️:<file>` from `LOGS_FOLDER`. The new `/sources` only scanned the folder — and here `LOGS_FOLDER=/tmp/codx-junior-logs` holds **1 file** while **21 containers** are running. That's why "the list of docker containers" disappeared.

Now `list_all_sources()` returns files **plus** containers as `kind="docker"`, id `docker:<name>`, read with `docker logs --tail`. Discovery is TTL-cached (5 s, `CODX_JUNIOR_LOG_EXPLORER_LOG_EXPLORER_CONTAINERS_TTL`), the runner is injectable, and a missing CLI/socket logs one warning and returns `[]` — never an exception. **New endpoint** `GET /api/logs/explorer/insights` → `summary` (requests, errors, error_rate, avg/p50/p95/p99/max ms), `histogram`, `endpoints`, `slowest`, `status`, `profiler`, `stats`. Plus `min_ms` on `/query` and `/insights`. Aggregation lives in `api/codx/junior/logs/insights.py` and reuses the existing bounded-window scan via a new shared `scan_entries()` — one pass, no duplicated reading.

**UI** — the explorer now opens on **API requests** (`Request`), not on a raw tail:

| Preset | Filter |
|---|---|
| **API requests** (default) | `Request` + insights panel |
| API errors | `Request` + `error,critical` |
| Slow API | `Request` + `≥500ms` |
| Profiler | `Profiler:` + insights |
| Errors & warnings | levels only |
| All logs | no filter |

`LogApiInsights.vue` shows KPI chips, the latency histogram (click = zoom), **top endpoints** table with error counts and p95 bars (click = filter by `"GET /api/chat"`), **slowest requests** (click = open the entry in the existing detail drawer), status distribution and profiler top methods. Source dropdown is now grouped **Containers / Files**; the empty state names the real cause instead of staying silent.

|---|---|
| `pytest tests/logs` | **121 passed** (was 99; +22 for docker, insights, anonymous-user regression) |
| `vite build` | **exit 0**, 5207 modules |
| `node --check` on changed JS | clean |
| No `v-html` in new/changed SFCs | yes — interpolation only |

The `codx-junior-api` process started **before** this code, and uvicorn runs **without reload** (by design — this chat runs inside that container, so I must not restart it):

```bash

```

After that: Logs app → your containers appear under **Containers** → it opens straight into API analysis. Two honest caveats: the API panel has no collapse toggle yet (it's open on the API presets), and the earlier `/sources` 500 means nothing in this feature was ever exercised against the live process — the restart is the first real end-to-end run.

"""
API performance logs router – HTTP call metrics backed by raw JSONL files.

API call performance events are written by the ``record_api_call`` helper in
``codx.junior.app`` (from the timing middleware) and read/filtered here via
:class:`~codx.junior.api_logs.api_logs.ApiLogs`.

User-scoped endpoints return metrics filtered to the authenticated user.
Admin-only endpoints return metrics across all users and require the ``admin``
role (enforced via the ``require_admin`` dependency).

Route layout
------------
GET /api/api-logs/dates                 – list dates with recorded calls (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/summary               – aggregated summary (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/daily                 – time-series breakdown (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/by-endpoint           – grouped by endpoint (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/by-status             – grouped by status code (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/slowest               – slowest calls (own data)
GET /api/api-logs/errors                – failed calls (own data)

GET /api/api-logs/admin/dates           – list dates (all users)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/summary         – aggregated summary (all users)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/daily           – time-series breakdown (all users)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-endpoint     – grouped by endpoint (admin)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-status       – grouped by status code (admin)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-user         – grouped by user (admin)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-project      – grouped by project (admin)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/slowest         – slowest calls (admin)
GET /api/api-logs/admin/errors          – failed calls (admin)

Diagram
-------
```mermaid
graph TD
    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/summary| UserSummary
    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/by-endpoint| UserByEndpoint
    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/slowest| UserSlowest

    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/admin/summary| AdminSummary
    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-user| AdminByUser
    Client -->|GET /api/api-logs/admin/by-project| AdminByProject

    UserSummary --> ApiLogs
    UserByEndpoint --> ApiLogs
    UserSlowest --> ApiLogs
    AdminSummary --> ApiLogs
    AdminByUser --> ApiLogs
    AdminByProject --> ApiLogs
```
"""

import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query

from codx.junior.api import require_admin
from codx.junior.model.model import CodxUser
from codx.junior.security.user_management import get_authenticated_user
from codx.junior.globals import API_LOGS_DATA_PATH
from codx.junior.api_logs import ApiLogs

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api-logs", tags=["api-logs"])

DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 50
MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500

# ── Shared ApiLogs instance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_api_logs: Optional[ApiLogs] = None


def _get_api_logs() -> ApiLogs:
    """Return (or lazily create) the shared ApiLogs instance."""
    global _api_logs
    if _api_logs is None:
        _api_logs = ApiLogs(logs_path=API_LOGS_DATA_PATH)
    return _api_logs

```py api/codx/junior/api/log_explorer.py
"""
Log explorer router – Loki/Graylog-style exploration of the application logs.

This is the REST surface of :mod:`codx.junior.logs` (parser + query language)
and :mod:`codx.junior.logs.service` (query engine). Everything is server-side:
the browser sends filters and receives at most one page of entries plus the
aggregations it needs to render facets and the histogram, so it never
downloads a whole log file.

The legacy ``/api/system/logs`` endpoints and the AI request/response logs
(``/api/logs/*``) are untouched and keep working.

Route layout
------------
GET /api/logs/explorer/sources            – list the queryable log files
GET /api/logs/explorer/query              – filtered, paged query + histogram + facets
GET /api/logs/explorer/entry/{id}         – one entry with its verbatim raw text
GET /api/logs/explorer/context/{id}       – entries surrounding an entry
GET /api/logs/explorer/tail               – poll for new content (cursor based)

Diagram
-------
```mermaid
graph TD
    Client -->|GET /sources| Sources
    Client -->|GET /query| Query
    Client -->|GET /entry/:id| Entry
    Client -->|GET /context/:id| Context
    Client -->|GET /tail| Tail

    Sources --> list_sources["logs/sources.list_sources"]
    Query --> service["logs/service.query_logs"]
    Entry --> service
    Context --> service
    Tail --> service
    service --> sources["bounded tail window"]
    sources --> parsers["logs/parsers.parse_lines"]
    service --> query["logs/query.compile_query"]
```
"""

import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from codx.junior.logs import service
from codx.junior.model.model import CodxUser
from codx.junior.security.user_management import get_authenticated_user

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/logs/explorer", tags=["logs"])

# ── Response models (the frozen contract) ─────────────────────────────────────


class LogSourceModel(BaseModel):
    """A log file the explorer can query."""

    id: str = Field(description="Source id, sent back as the 'source' query param.")
    name: str = Field(description="Display name of the source.")
    path: str = Field(description="Absolute path of the log file.")
    size_bytes: int = Field(default=0, description="File size in bytes.")
    mtime: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Last modification time, epoch seconds.")
    kind: str = Field(default="log", description="Source kind: jsonl | log | text.")
    entries_estimate: int = Field(default=0, description="Estimated number of lines.")


class SourcesResponse(BaseModel):
    """Payload of ``GET /sources``."""

    sources: List[LogSourceModel] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Queryable sources.")


class LogEntryModel(BaseModel):
    """One parsed log entry as returned by the list endpoints."""

    id: str = Field(description="Stable synthetic id: '<source>#<line index>'.")
    timestamp: str = Field(default="", description="Timestamp as printed in the log.")
    ts_ms: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, description="Timestamp in epoch milliseconds.")
    level: str = Field(default="unknown", description="Canonical level name.")
    logger: str = Field(default="", description="Logger name from the header.")
    module: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Module from the header.")
    line: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, description="Source line number.")
    message: str = Field(default="", description="Message body, continuations included.")
    fields: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Structured extras.")
    continuation_lines: int = Field(default=0, description="Number of continuation lines.")
    source: str = Field(default="", description="Source id the entry comes from.")
    raw_preview: str = Field(default="", description="First raw line, truncated.")


class LogEntryDetailModel(LogEntryModel):
    """One entry with its verbatim raw text (``GET /entry/{id}``)."""

    raw: str = Field(default="", description="Verbatim text of the entry.")


class HistogramBucketModel(BaseModel):
    """One time bucket of the query histogram."""

    ts_ms: int = Field(description="Bucket start, epoch milliseconds.")
    total: int = Field(default=0, description="Entries in the bucket.")
    by_level: Dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Count per level.")


class FacetValueModel(BaseModel):
    """A facet value with its number of entries."""

    value: str = Field(description="Facet value (level, logger or module).")
    count: int = Field(default=0, description="Number of matched entries.")


class FacetsModel(BaseModel):
    """Aggregations over the matched set."""

    level: List[FacetValueModel] = Field(default_factory=list)
    logger: List[FacetValueModel] = Field(default_factory=list)
    module: List[FacetValueModel] = Field(default_factory=list)


class QueryStatsModel(BaseModel):
    """Cost and completeness of the scan behind a query response."""

    scanned_lines: int = Field(default=0, description="Lines parsed for this query.")
    scanned_bytes: int = Field(default=0, description="Bytes read for this query.")
    matched: int = Field(default=0, description="Entries matching the query.")
    duration_ms: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Server processing time, milliseconds.")
    truncated: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="True when only the tail window of a bigger file was scanned.",
    )


class QueryResponse(BaseModel):
    """Payload of ``GET /query``."""

    entries: List[LogEntryModel] = Field(default_factory=list)
    total: int = Field(default=0, description="Total number of matched entries.")
    page: int = Field(default=1, description="Current page (1-based).")
    page_size: int = Field(default=service.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, description="Entries per page.")
    has_more: bool = Field(default=False, description="True when another page exists.")
    histogram: List[HistogramBucketModel] = Field(default_factory=list)
    facets: FacetsModel = Field(default_factory=FacetsModel)
    stats: QueryStatsModel = Field(default_factory=QueryStatsModel)


class ContextResponse(BaseModel):
    """Payload of ``GET /context/{id}``."""

    entries: List[LogEntryModel] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TailResponse(BaseModel):
    """Payload of ``GET /tail``."""

    cursor: str = Field(default="0", description="Opaque cursor to send back on the next poll.")
    entries: List[LogEntryModel] = Field(default_factory=list)


# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _username(user: Optional[CodxUser]) -> str:
    """
    Return the username of *user*, tolerating an unauthenticated session.

    ``get_authenticated_user`` returns ``None`` (it does not raise) when the
    request carries no valid ``authentication`` header, so the explorer must
    never dereference the user blindly: doing so turned every route into a
    500 ``AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'username'`` and
    the UI rendered an empty source list.

    Args:
        user: Authenticated user, or ``None`` for an anonymous request.

    Returns:
        The username, or ``"anonymous"`` when there is none.
    """
    return getattr(user, "username", None) or "anonymous"


def _existing_sources(source: List[str], user: CodxUser) -> List[str]:
    """
    Validate the requested source ids against the available log files.

    Args:
        source: Source ids requested by the client (may be empty).
        user:   Authenticated user (for the log line).

    Returns:
        The requested ids (empty when the client did not filter by source).

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: When one of the requested sources does not exist.
    """
    requested = [source_id for source_id in (source or []) if source_id]
    if not requested:
        return []
    available = {entry["id"] for entry in service.list_available_sources()}
    missing = [source_id for source_id in requested if source_id not in available]
    if missing:
        logger.warning("Log explorer: user %s asked for unknown sources %s", _username(user), missing)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown log source: {', '.join(missing)}")
    return requested


# ── Endpoints ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@router.get("/sources", response_model=SourcesResponse, summary="List queryable application log sources")
def api_log_explorer_sources(
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> SourcesResponse:
    """
    List the application log files the explorer can query.

    The folder is the same one the legacy ``/api/system/logs`` endpoint lists
    (``CODX_JUNIOR_API_LOGS``). Sources are returned newest first.

    Returns:
        ``{"sources": [{id, name, path, size_bytes, mtime, kind, entries_estimate}]}``
    """
    sources = service.list_available_sources()
    logger.debug("Log explorer: %d sources for user %s", len(sources), _username(user))
    return SourcesResponse(sources=[LogSourceModel(**source) for source in sources])


@router.get("/query", response_model=QueryResponse, summary="Query log entries (server-side filtering and pagination)")
def api_log_explorer_query(
    source: List[str] = Query(
        default=[],
        description="Source id, repeatable. Defaults to the newest log file.",
    ),
    q: str = Query(
        "",
        description=(
            "Query text: free text, \"exact phrase\", level=error,warn, "
            "logger~\"regex\", field=value and -negation, AND-joined."
        ),
    ),
    start: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Inclusive start: epoch ms/s or ISO-8601."),
    end: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Inclusive end: epoch ms/s or ISO-8601."),
    level: List[str] = Query(
        default=[],
        description="Level filter, repeatable (critical|error|warn|info|debug|trace).",
    ),
    page: int = Query(1, ge=1, description="Page number (1-based)."),
    page_size: int = Query(
        service.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE,
        ge=1,
        le=service.MAX_PAGE_SIZE,
        description="Entries per page (max 1000).",
    ),
    order: str = Query("desc", pattern="^(asc|desc)$", description="Sort order by timestamp."),
    histogram_buckets: int = Query(
        service.DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS,
        ge=1,
        le=service.MAX_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS,
        description="Number of histogram buckets.",
    ),
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> QueryResponse:
    """
    Query one or more log sources.

    Filtering, sorting, aggregation and pagination are all server-side: the
    response never carries more than ``page_size`` entries.

    Returns:
        ``{entries, total, page, page_size, has_more, histogram, facets, stats}``

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: When a requested source does not exist.
    """
    requested = _existing_sources(source, user)
    result = service.query_logs(
        requested,
        q=q,
        start=start,
        end=end,
        levels=level,
        page=page,
        page_size=page_size,
        order=order,
        histogram_buckets=histogram_buckets,
    )
    logger.info(
        "Log explorer: user %s queried %s (q=%r) -> %d/%d entries in %.2f ms",
        _username(user), requested or "newest", q, len(result["entries"]),
        result["total"], result["stats"]["duration_ms"],
    )
    return QueryResponse(**result)


@router.get("/entry/{id}", response_model=LogEntryDetailModel, summary="Full log entry with its raw text")
def api_log_explorer_entry(
    id: str,
    source: Optional[str] = Query(
        None,
        description="Source id; taken from the entry id when omitted.",
    ),
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> LogEntryDetailModel:
    """
    Return one log entry including its verbatim ``raw`` text.

    Args:
        id:     Entry id (``<source>#<line index>``) as returned by ``/query``.
        source: Optional source id, when the id lost its source part.

    Returns:
        The full entry.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: When the entry is not in the scanned window.
    """
    entry = service.get_entry(entry_id=id, source=source)
    if entry is None:
        logger.info("Log explorer: user %s requested a missing entry %r", _username(user), id)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Log entry '{id}' not found.")
    return LogEntryDetailModel(**entry)


@router.get("/context/{id}", response_model=ContextResponse, summary="Entries surrounding a log entry")
def api_log_explorer_context(
    id: str,
    source: Optional[str] = Query(
        None,
        description="Source id; taken from the entry id when omitted.",
    ),
    before: int = Query(10, ge=0, le=500, description="Preceding entries."),
    after: int = Query(10, ge=0, le=500, description="Following entries."),
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> ContextResponse:
    """
    Return the entries surrounding *id* (in ascending file order).

    Args:
        id:     Entry id used as the anchor.
        source: Optional source id, when the id lost its source part.
        before: How many preceding entries to include.
        after:  How many following entries to include.

    Returns:
        ``{"entries": [...]}``

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: When the anchor entry is not in the scanned window.
    """
    context = service.get_context(entry_id=id, source=source, before=before, after=after)
    if context is None:
        logger.info("Log explorer: user %s requested context of a missing entry %r", _username(user), id)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Log entry '{id}' not found.")
    return ContextResponse(**context)


@router.get("/tail", response_model=TailResponse, summary="Poll a log source for new entries")
def api_log_explorer_tail(
    source: Optional[str] = Query(
        None,
        description="Source id; defaults to the newest log file.",
    ),
    since_cursor: Optional[str] = Query(
        None,
        description="Cursor returned by the previous poll (byte offset).",
    ),
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> TailResponse:
    """
    Poll a log source.

    Without ``since_cursor`` the last window of the file is returned. With a
    cursor only the bytes appended after it are parsed; send the returned
    ``cursor`` back on the next poll.

    Args:
        source:       Source id (defaults to the newest log file).
        since_cursor: Cursor returned by the previous poll.

    Returns:
        ``{cursor, entries}``

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: When no source (or the requested one) exists.
    """
    if source:
        _existing_sources([source], user)
    result = service.tail(source=source, since_cursor=since_cursor)
    if result is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown log source: {source or '(none)'}")
    logger.debug(
        "Log explorer: tail %s since %r -> %d entries (cursor %s)",
        source or "newest", since_cursor, len(result["entries"]), result["cursor"],
    )
    return TailResponse(**result)

# ── Scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Window:
    """Parsed snapshot of one source: the bounded tail window as entries."""

    source: LogSource
    entries: List[LogEntry]
    scanned_lines: int
    scanned_bytes: int
    truncated: bool


def _read_window(source: LogSource, max_bytes: int) -> _Window:
    """
    Read and parse the bounded tail window of *source*.

    Args:
        source:    The log source to read.
        max_bytes: Size of the byte window taken from the end of the file.

    Returns:
        The parsed :class:`_Window` (empty when the file vanished).
    """
    try:
        read = read_tail(source.path, max_bytes=max_bytes)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.warning("Log explorer: cannot read %s: %s", source.path, ex)
        return _Window(source=source, entries=[], scanned_lines=0, scanned_bytes=0, truncated=False)

    start_index = estimate_line_index(source.path, read.start_offset)
    entries = parse_lines(read.lines, source=source.id, start_index=start_index)
    return _Window(
        source=source,
        entries=entries,
        scanned_lines=len(read.lines),
        scanned_bytes=read.bytes_read,
        truncated=read.truncated,
    )


def _resolve_sources(
    sources: Optional[Sequence[str]],
    folder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[LogSource]:
    """
    Resolve the requested source ids to :class:`LogSource` objects.

    An empty selection means "the newest log file", which is what an explorer
    opens by default. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning (the file may have
    rotated away between two polls) instead of failing the whole query.

    Args:
        sources: Requested source ids (file names), possibly empty.
        folder:  Folder to scan; defaults to the configured log folder.

    Returns:
        The sources to scan, at most :data:`MAX_SOURCES_PER_QUERY`.
    """
    available = list_sources(folder)
    if not available:
        return []

    wanted = [source_id for source_id in (sources or []) if source_id]
    if not wanted:
        return available[:1]

    by_id = {source.id: source for source in available}
    selected: List[LogSource] = []
    for source_id in wanted[:MAX_SOURCES_PER_QUERY]:
        source = by_id.get(source_id)
        if source is None:
            logger.warning("Log explorer: source %r not found, skipping it", source_id)
            continue
        if source not in selected:
            selected.append(source)
    return selected

def _sort_key(entry: LogEntry) -> Tuple[int, int, str]:
    """Sort key: timestamp (entries without one go last), then header line."""
    return (
        entry.ts_ms if entry.ts_ms is not None else -1,
        entry.line if entry.line is not None else 0,
        entry.id,
    )


def _in_range(entry: LogEntry, start_ms: Optional[int], end_ms: Optional[int]) -> bool:
    """
    Return ``True`` when *entry* falls inside the ``[start_ms, end_ms]`` range.

def _scan_limit() -> int:

    call so it can be tuned without a restart) and falls back to
    :data:`DEFAULT_SCAN_BYTES`.

    Returns:
        The scan window in bytes, never smaller than :data:`MIN_SCAN_BYTES`.
    """
    raw = os.environ.get(SCAN_BYTES_ENV)
    try:
        value = int(raw) if raw else DEFAULT_SCAN_BYTES
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("Invalid %s=%r, using %d bytes", SCAN_BYTES_ENV, raw, DEFAULT_SCAN_BYTES)
        value = DEFAULT_SCAN_BYTES

    try:
        value = int(page_size) if page_size is not None else DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        value = DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
    return max(1, min(value, MAX_PAGE_SIZE))


def _clamp_buckets(buckets: Optional[int]) -> int:
    """Clamp the histogram bucket count to ``[1, MAX_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS]``."""
    try:
        value = int(buckets) if buckets is not None else DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        value = DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS
    return max(1, min(value, MAX_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS))


def to_epoch_ms(value: Any) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Convert a time bound to epoch milliseconds.

    Accepts epoch seconds, epoch milliseconds, numeric strings and ISO-8601
    timestamps, so the frontend can send whatever a date picker produced.

    Args:
        value: Time bound (``None``/``""`` means "no bound").

    Returns:
        The bound in epoch milliseconds, or ``None`` when it is absent or
        cannot be parsed.

    if value is None or isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        number = float(value)
    else:
        text = str(value).strip()
        if not text:
            return None
        try:
            number = float(text)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return parse_timestamp_ms(text)

    if number <= 0:
        return None

    return int(number if number >= 1e11 else number * 1000)

    """Return the first line of the entry, truncated to ``RAW_PREVIEW_CHARS``."""

    if len(first_line) > RAW_PREVIEW_CHARS:
        return first_line[:RAW_PREVIEW_CHARS] + "..."
    return first_line

        "timestamp": entry.timestamp,
        "ts_ms": entry.ts_ms,
        "level": entry.level,
        "logger": entry.logger,
        "module": entry.module,

def _resolve_sources(
    sources: Optional[Sequence[str]],
    folder: Optional[str] = None,

    """
    Resolve the requested source ids to :class:`LogSource` objects.

    An empty selection means "the newest log file", which is what an explorer
    opens by default. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning (the file may have
    rotated away between two polls) instead of failing the whole query.

    Args:
        sources: Requested source ids (file names), possibly empty.
        folder:  Folder to scan; defaults to the configured log folder.

    Returns:

    if not available:

# ── Predicates & aggregations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _sort_key(entry: LogEntry) -> Tuple[int, int, str]:
    """Sort key: timestamp (entries without one go last), then header line."""
    return (
        entry.ts_ms if entry.ts_ms is not None else -1,
        entry.line if entry.line is not None else 0,
        entry.id,
    )


def _in_range(entry: LogEntry, start_ms: Optional[int], end_ms: Optional[int]) -> bool:
    """
    Return ``True`` when *entry* falls inside the ``[start_ms, end_ms]`` range.

    Entries without a parsable timestamp are only kept when no bound was given:
    they cannot be placed on the timeline.
    """
    if start_ms is None and end_ms is None:
        return True
    if entry.ts_ms is None:
        return False
    if start_ms is not None and entry.ts_ms < start_ms:
        return False
    if end_ms is not None and entry.ts_ms > end_ms:
        return False
    return True


def _build_histogram(
    entries: Sequence[LogEntry],
    start_ms: Optional[int],
    end_ms: Optional[int],
    buckets: int,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Build evenly spaced time buckets over the matched entries.

    Args:
        entries: Entries matched by the query (already filtered).
        start_ms: Range start (``None`` → earliest matched timestamp).
        end_ms:   Range end (``None`` → latest matched timestamp).
        buckets:  Number of buckets.

    Returns:
        One ``{ts_ms, total, by_level}`` dict per bucket, oldest first; an empty
        list when no entry carries a timestamp.
    """
    timestamps = [entry.ts_ms for entry in entries if entry.ts_ms is not None]
    if not timestamps:
        return []

    buckets = _clamp_buckets(buckets)
    low = start_ms if start_ms is not None else min(timestamps)
    high = end_ms if end_ms is not None else max(timestamps)
    if high < low:
        low, high = high, low

    span = max(1, high - low)
    width = max(1.0, span / buckets)
    histogram: List[Dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"ts_ms": int(low + index * width), "total": 0, "by_level": {}}
        for index in range(buckets)
    ]

    for entry in entries:
        if entry.ts_ms is None:
            continue
        position = int((entry.ts_ms - low) / width)
        position = 0 if position < 0 else (buckets - 1 if position >= buckets else position)
        bucket = histogram[position]
        bucket["total"] += 1
        bucket["by_level"][entry.level] = bucket["by_level"].get(entry.level, 0) + 1

    return histogram


def _facet_values(counter: Counter) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the ``FACET_LIMIT`` most frequent values of *counter*."""
    ordered = sorted(counter.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], str(item[0])))
    return [{"value": value, "count": count} for value, count in ordered[:FACET_LIMIT]]


def _build_facets(entries: Sequence[LogEntry]) -> Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
    """
    Build the level/logger/module facets over the matched entries.

    Args:
        entries: Entries matched by the query (before pagination).

    Returns:
        ``{"level": [...], "logger": [...], "module": [...]}`` with
        ``{value, count}`` items, most frequent first.
    """
    counters: Dict[str, Counter] = {
        "level": Counter(),
        "logger": Counter(),
        "module": Counter(),
    }
    for entry in entries:
        counters["level"][entry.level or "unknown"] += 1
        if entry.logger:
            counters["logger"][entry.logger] += 1
        if entry.module:
            counters["module"][entry.module] += 1
    return {name: _facet_values(counter) for name, counter in counters.items()}

    q: str = "",
    start: Any = None,
    end: Any = None,
    levels: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    page: int = 1,
    page_size: int = DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE,
    order: str = "desc",
    histogram_buckets: int = DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS,
    folder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Query one or more log sources and return the frozen response payload.

    Filtering, sorting, aggregation and pagination all happen here: the client
    never receives more than ``page_size`` entries (capped at
    :data:`MAX_PAGE_SIZE`) and never a whole log file.

    Args:
        sources:          Source ids to scan; empty means "the newest file".
        q:                Query text (see :mod:`codx.junior.logs.query`).
        start:            Inclusive time-range start (epoch s/ms or ISO-8601).
        end:              Inclusive time-range end (epoch s/ms or ISO-8601).
        levels:           Level filter (canonical or raw level names).
        page:             1-based page number.
        page_size:        Entries per page (clamped to ``[1, MAX_PAGE_SIZE]``).
        order:            ``desc`` (newest first, default) or ``asc``.
        histogram_buckets: Number of histogram buckets.
        folder:           Log folder override (defaults to the configured one).

    Returns:
        ``{entries, total, page, page_size, has_more, histogram, facets, stats}``
        exactly as documented by the ``/api/logs/explorer/query`` contract.
    """
    started = time.perf_counter()

    query = compile_query(q)
    level_filter = {
        normalize_level(level) for level in (levels or []) if str(level).strip()
    }
    start_ms = to_epoch_ms(start)
    end_ms = to_epoch_ms(end)
    page = max(1, int(page or 1))
    page_size = _clamp_page_size(page_size)
    buckets = _clamp_buckets(histogram_buckets)
    descending = str(order or "desc").lower() != "asc"

    matched: List[LogEntry] = []
    scanned_lines = 0
    scanned_bytes = 0
    truncated = False

    for source in _resolve_sources(sources, folder):
        window = _read_window(source, _scan_limit())
        scanned_lines += window.scanned_lines
        scanned_bytes += window.scanned_bytes
        truncated = truncated or window.truncated
        for entry in window.entries:
            if level_filter and entry.level not in level_filter:
                continue
            if not _in_range(entry, start_ms, end_ms):
                continue
            if not query.matches(entry):
                continue
            matched.append(entry)

    matched.sort(key=_sort_key, reverse=descending)
    total = len(matched)
    offset = (page - 1) * page_size
    page_entries = matched[offset:offset + page_size]
    duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000.0, 2)

    logger.debug(
        "query_logs: q=%r levels=%s range=%s..%s matched=%d scanned=%d lines/%d bytes "
        "page=%d/%d in %.2f ms",

        scanned_bytes, page, page_size, duration_ms,
    )

        "entries": [entry_to_dict(entry) for entry in page_entries],
        "total": total,
        "page": page,
        "page_size": page_size,
        "has_more": offset + len(page_entries) < total,
        "histogram": _build_histogram(matched, start_ms, end_ms, buckets),
        "facets": _build_facets(matched),
        "stats": {

            "scanned_bytes": scanned_bytes,
            "matched": total,
            "duration_ms": duration_ms,
            "truncated": truncated,

def _split_entry_id(entry_id: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[int]]:
    """
    Split ``"<source>#<index>"`` into its parts.

    Args:
        entry_id: Entry id produced by :func:`codx.junior.logs.parsers.parse_lines`.

    Returns:
        ``(source_id, index)`` — ``index`` is ``None`` when it is not numeric.
    """
    source_id, _separator, raw_index = (entry_id or "").rpartition("#")
    try:
        return source_id, int(raw_index)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):

def _find_entry(
    entry_id: str,
    source: Optional[str] = None,
    folder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Optional[LogEntry]:
    """
    Resolve an entry id against a freshly parsed window of its source.

    Args:
        entry_id: The entry id (``<source>#<line index>``).
        source:   Optional source override (when the id lost its source part).
        folder:   Log folder override.

    Returns:
        The matching entry, or ``None`` when it is not in the scanned window.

        return None

    window = _read_window(log_source, _scan_limit())

        source:   Optional source override.

        The full entry dict, or ``None`` when it cannot be found.

def get_context(
    entry_id: str,
    source: Optional[str] = None,
    before: int = 10,
    after: int = 10,
    folder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Return the entries surrounding *entry_id* (in file order).

    Args:
        entry_id: The anchor entry id.
        source:   Optional source override.
        before:   How many preceding entries to include.
        after:    How many following entries to include.
        folder:   Log folder override.

    Returns:
        ``{"entries": [...]}`` in ascending file order, or ``None`` when the
        anchor entry is not in the scanned window.
    """
    source_id, _index = _split_entry_id(entry_id)
    log_source = get_source(source or source_id, folder)
    if log_source is None:
        logger.debug("get_context: unknown source for id %r", entry_id)
        return None

    window = _read_window(log_source, _scan_limit())
    position = next(
        (index for index, entry in enumerate(window.entries) if entry.id == entry_id),
        None,
    )
    if position is None:
        logger.debug("get_context: id %r not found in %s", entry_id, log_source.path)
        return None

    before = max(0, int(before or 0))
    after = max(0, int(after or 0))
    selection = window.entries[max(0, position - before):position + after + 1]
    return {"entries": [entry_to_dict(entry) for entry in selection]}


def _to_cursor(since_cursor: Any) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Parse a ``/tail`` cursor (a byte offset, optionally with a ``b`` prefix).

    Args:
        since_cursor: Cursor returned by a previous ``/tail`` call.

    Returns:
        The byte offset, or ``None`` when the cursor is absent/unusable.
    """
    if since_cursor is None:
        return None
    text = str(since_cursor).strip().lstrip("b")
    if not text:
        return None
    try:
        return max(0, int(float(text)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.debug("tail: ignoring invalid cursor %r", since_cursor)
        return None


def tail(
    source: Optional[str] = None,
    since_cursor: Any = None,
    folder: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Poll a log source for new content (byte-offset cursor based).

    Without a cursor the last window of the file is returned (``tail -n``
    behaviour). With a cursor only the bytes written after it are parsed, and a
    partially written last line is left for the next poll. A cursor greater than
    the file size means the file was rotated/truncated: the cursor is reset and
    the current tail is returned.

    Args:
        source:       Source id; defaults to the newest log file.
        since_cursor: Cursor returned by the previous poll.
        folder:       Log folder override.

    Returns:
        ``{"cursor": "<new offset>", "entries": [...]}``, or ``None`` when the
        source does not exist.
    """
    if source:
        log_source = get_source(source, folder)
    else:
        available = list_sources(folder)
        log_source = available[0] if available else None
    if log_source is None:
        return None

    try:
        size = os.path.getsize(log_source.path)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.warning("tail: cannot stat %s: %s", log_source.path, ex)
        return None

    cursor = _to_cursor(since_cursor)
    max_bytes = _scan_limit()

    if cursor is None or cursor <= 0 or cursor > size:
        if cursor is not None and cursor > size:
            logger.info(
                "tail: %s rotated or truncated (cursor %d > size %d), resetting",
                log_source.id, cursor, size,
            )
        read = read_tail(log_source.path, max_bytes=max_bytes)
        start_index = estimate_line_index(log_source.path, read.start_offset)
        entries = parse_lines(read.lines, source=log_source.id, start_index=start_index)
        logger.debug("tail: initial read of %s returned %d entries", log_source.id, len(entries))
        return {
            "cursor": str(size),
            "entries": [entry_to_dict(entry) for entry in entries[-MAX_TAIL_ENTRIES:]],
        }

    start = max(cursor, size - max_bytes)
    try:
        data = read_range(log_source.path, start, size - start)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.warning("tail: cannot read %s: %s", log_source.path, ex)
        return {"cursor": str(cursor), "entries": []}

    cut = data.rfind(b"\n")
    if cut < 0:
        # Only a partially written line: keep the cursor where it was.
        logger.debug("tail: no complete line after %d in %s", start, log_source.id)
        return {"cursor": str(start), "entries": []}

    consumed = data[:cut + 1]
    lines = split_log_lines(consumed)
    start_index = estimate_line_index(log_source.path, start)
    entries = parse_lines(lines, source=log_source.id, start_index=start_index)
    new_cursor = start + len(consumed)
    logger.debug(
        "tail: %s %d new bytes -> %d entries", log_source.id, len(consumed), len(entries)
    )
    return {
        "cursor": str(new_cursor),
        "entries": [entry_to_dict(entry) for entry in entries[-MAX_TAIL_ENTRIES:]],
    }

    Return the serialised list of queryable sources.

    Args:
        folder: Log folder override.

    Returns:
        A list of ``LogSource`` dicts, newest first.
    """
    return [source.model_dump() for source in list_sources(folder)]
